utterances.text: Prior to your assignment as an operator, did you hold any other position in the army of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now, have you had an opportunity to review a packet containing three tabs of intercepted communications?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And in particular, did you review the handwritten material that's contained in the packet?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And did you recognise the handwriting in two of the three tabs as that of your own?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And was that in relation to two intercepted communications that occurred on 15th July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, did you transcribe or write that material into a notebook pursuant to your responsibilities and duties as an intercept operator assigned to the southern site of the Anti-Electronic Warfare Unit?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And have you had an opportunity to review the original notebook containing these handwritten intercepts?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Are you satisfied that the copies of the two intercepts that are yours contained in the packet conform to the originals that you reviewed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And were you able to -- were you able to confirm the date of the two intercepts transcribed in the original notebook as the 15th July 1995?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: May I have -- I'd like to put one of the original notebooks, please, on the ELMO. That is PO2242. For the record, the ERN number of the page displayed should be 0080-1719. Okay. Can we zoom out just a little bit, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. If you could just indicate for the record, and for the benefit of the Court, is that your handwriting that's depicted below the date?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And, in fact, is that your handwriting that -- did you write the date that appears on that particular page?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: The date and everything else is in my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. I would just like to draw your attention to a couple of things. Is it possible to have the English translation which is 65 ter 1172A displayed, please? Thank you. Witness, I would just like to draw your attention to something that appears in your notebook that has been translated as, "Did the cork pop anywhere," which is on the top right-hand side of the English translation as it appears, also on the top right-hand side of the page of your notebook. Are you able to see your notebook on the monitor? Okay. Could you indicate where that phrase appears in your notebook? If you could just -- I think you can point to it, put your finger underneath and show us where it appears.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes, it's there, you can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Now you've pointed to a part of the text that appears to be -- oops, okay. About four lines down. Could you point to it once again so we can see clearly exactly where it is?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: [Indicates].

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. You're indicating a mark that you placed in your notebook; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us what that mark corresponds to on the page of your notebook as it's displayed before you now?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: When you are writing a text out, some things sometimes you don't hear all that well. I didn't understand very well what was said at that point, and so I put an asterisk there. And then I continued to work on it. When I was finished transcribing with the -- the whole text, I went back to that part again and with the help of my colleagues, I managed to decipher what was said. And this was then written later at the top, at the top of the text. And the asterisks were -- was placed there as a reminder for people who were typing the text out later, where that part is supposed to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And is that part supposed to go where you've placed the asterisk or below where you've placed the asterisk?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: That part goes just underneath the place where I put the asterisk. The last part that is written actually is said by one person, the sentence ends there. Then another person, there are different initials in front of the next, so that part of the text is spoken by another person underneath.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that part of the text the phrase, "Did the cork pop anywhere?" Or something to that effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. The portion that corresponds to the asterisk, is that located on the top right where you initially pointed, of this page? Just beneath the date on the right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: That part is supposed to go into a new line.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Is that part -- is that part translated as, "Did the cork pop anywhere?" Or something to that effect?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can I just refer you -- if we could just pull out, zoom out for just a little bit and go down the page. A little further down, please. Just -- exactly. Down the page. That's right. Okay. In the lower part of the page there appear to be a series of statements that aren't attributed a particular letter or anything of that nature. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: That begins somewhere around -- is where the statement is, "Is Golic there?"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Can you tell us in sequence who -- who the following statements should be attributed to in your notebook transcription?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: I do not wish to state this openly. Can we please move to private session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'll do my best. I'm not sure I quite recall it.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think I'd asked whether you could tell us who the collocutors are following the reference in the text of your handwritten materials to the statement, "Is Golic there?"

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: After that question, Mijatovic came on.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. And following -- following that, can you tell us if there are any other statements that should be attributed to either P, which you've indicated here is Pandurevic, or M, meaning Mijatovic or Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: As the text continues, the conversation is between Pandurevic and Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: So the record is clear, the statement or question from below, do you see that in your text?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: "Is Golic there?" Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. "Is Golic there?" You see that in your text. The next statement, "Here, the old places, Jasikovci, Planinci, and there's a statement following that, "Are there any infiltrated groups?" Do you see that in your text?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Who should that be attributed to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: To Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Then there appears to be a response that says, "From below?" Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: That is -- just one moment, please. That is more a question than an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, can you say if you recall who is asking it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Pandurevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Can you go to the next line and just tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Mijatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: The next question, "From which battalion?" Is that attributable to Mr. Pandurevic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: And the statement following that, is that attributable to Mr. Mijatovic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Could I just have briefly the page turned on - - in the notebook to ERN number 1 -- ending 1721? And that corresponds to tab 3 in the packet. 1721, please. Okay. Thank you. The first two lines of this particular intercept don't appear to be attributed to anybody. Can you tell us, so the record is clear, who those lines should be attributable to, or attributed to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: The first speaker is Pandurevic. The second speaker is Jokic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you for that. I have no further questions at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Vanderpuye. Mr. Zivanovic, I understand you want to cross-examine the witness. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: Yesterday you gave a statement to the Prosecutor. I would just like you to clarify a couple of things. You said in the statement, among other things, that at the location where you were there were two or three sets of equipment usually; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: You said that you worked in shifts of four hours each; is that correct? And you said that two operators worked in the shifts from 6.00 in the morning until 10.00 at night; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read exactly what it says in the translation of the statement. "Two operators worked in a shift during the day from 0600 to 2200 hours." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Two in shifts, in shifts of four hours each.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read the previous sentence also. "Normally, we were using two or three sets and we worked in shifts for four hours. Two intercept operators were working in one shift during the day from 6.00 a.m. until 10.00 p.m., one operator during the night from 10.00 p.m. until 6.00 a.m." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: I would like to know whether this also applies to 1995, since I couldn't see that from the statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: My last question, if you can recall, is this: Do you know exactly what type of antennae was used at the facility?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZIVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, no further questions. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Zivanovic. I would like to confirm the Beara team that you have no cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. We have no questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Meek. The Nikolic team?

utterances.speaker: MS. NIKOLIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Nikolic. The Borovcanin team.

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: No cross-examine, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I understand Madam Fauveau has a cross- examination for the witness. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a question. Could we possibly come back to pages 201719 of the notebook? It's P2242. Could we show the part in which the names of participants are missing? It's towards the bottom. Perfect. Sir, can you explain why you didn't put down the initials of the persons speaking at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: And can you explain why you didn't put them down?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Simply because I was trying to work as fast as I could, and each new participant receives a new line and a new initial.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: Do you know whether other operators always -- or rather did the same thing, which is not to always note the initials?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Madam Fauveau. I take it that the Gvero team haven't got any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Confirmed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And same as regards the Pandurevic team?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Your Honour, yes. Or no, rather.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is there any re-examination, Mr. Vanderpuye?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I think I have just one follow-up question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I previously referred you to page ERN number 1719, where you indicated for the Court the sequence in which the conversation unfolded. Were you able to compare that to the printed version of that intercept and is the printed version correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-151
utterances.text: Both yes and no.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Well, is it correct with respect to the particular sequence that you described for the Court as to the speakers?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. Objection. This is a suggestive question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, perhaps also apart from that, Mr. Vanderpuye had explained to us how his question is rooted in the -- to the cross- examinations.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: I'm sorry? I think it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why do you consider this is a re-examination? Where does it flow from?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: It flows from my colleague's question concerning the practice of not noting down or some intercept operators not noting down particular participants in a given sequence, and I'm merely asking the witness whether or not he can confirm that the sequence he relayed to the Court is accurate, one, given what he's examined, which is his notebook, and he's -- and I'm asking whether or not he's examined a printout and whether or not that's -- the sequence was correct with respect to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you have already asked him that, but I think we can stop there, Mr. Vanderpuye.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Very well, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No further questions, I take it. Judge Kwon, Judge Prost, Judge Stole. Sir, your testimony comes to an end here. I wish to thank you for having come over to give evidence. Our staff will assist you and help you return back over at the earliest. On behalf of everyone here, I wish you a safe journey back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed with the documents tendering process.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let me help you and get it over --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: -- quickly. There are two documents that the Prosecution wishes to tender. One is the witness statement and the other one is the pseudonym sheet. They are both being admitted under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then there are intercepts, three intercepts, as per the list, that has been --

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: There will be only two, Mr. President. In sequence, that is at tab 2 and tab 3, ERN numbers -- I'm sorry, the 65 ter number 1172, A through D. And 1174, A through D. My understanding is that the notebook is in evidence already -- I mean has been tendered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And then there are handwritten notebooks number 15 and 101 which, according to you, have already been tendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. VANDERPUYE
utterances.text: Yes. In relation to this particular witness though, only notebook 101 should really be considered, because...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. It's two intercepts plus one notebook. I hear no objection. They will be marked for identification purposes for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I mean Madam Registrar is informing me that Prosecution haven't made it -- that some of -- there will be tendered under seal. I leave it in your hands. You liaise with the registrar, and we don't need to get involved in that any further. Now, we -- where do we stand, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, we have one more witness. I will be leading that witness, but it will be extremely short on direct. The -- he is a member of the 21st Division, which we haven't had before, but it still will be very short on direct. And that was the last witness we had planned, based on our -- our judgement of the previous witnesses, which I apologise, was just wrong. And we didn't keep -- we didn't catch up with the Court's ruling in time. I've looked into getting people here to make up for that, and I have been unable to. It's complicated, but as you know, it is a question of visas and bringing people around. I know how serious this is, I hate to waste even a moment on a Friday, but that's where we are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the next witness, is he available now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, the witness is arriving from Bosnia tonight. I will be seeing the witness in the morning and be giving a brief statement in both languages to counsel, hopefully around noon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I think there is no other alternative for the time being. In the meantime, assuming, if I read you well, that we won't need the entire sitting of tomorrow to finish this -- with this -- with this next witness, I would suggest again reiterate what I suggested earlier, that you try to liaise the two sides, the two parties, to see if and how we could utilise in a profitable way the time remaining tomorrow and also Friday morning. If you can find a common denominator or common ground, please come back. But we can visit that again tomorrow. In the meantime, I think we have no option for today except to adjourn. I don't think -- yes, Madam Fauveau? She's raising something to keep us occupied for two days.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. I apologise. I was waiting for the French translation to be through. I am slightly concerned about the witness arriving tomorrow. If we manage to organise things so easily today, because this witness was repeating or not repeating what the other witness said today, but even if it wasn't the same witness, so the witness coming tomorrow is a witness who comes from the 21st Division and we have no idea what this witness will be talking about. We might not have any problems but we might request what I already requested today which is that if there are any new things, new topics raised tomorrow in this witness's statement that we have a chance to cross- examine this witness on Friday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll play it by the ear. We have to wait -- we know even less than you do what this witness will be stating. So Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: He is an intercept operator, it's the same story, I can't imagine much that would be new. Obviously it is a different unit, so questions about what might be different are appropriate, but this is the same thing. So I don't imagine it will be much different. It won't be much different with the MUP, either. But they may want to explore that area. Obviously, I'll try to get that out briefly, if I can, but I don't know of any major differences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As I said, we will play it by ear and we will see tomorrow. You know that the system -- the practice of this Trial Chamber is not to close doors as much as possible unless we detect wasting of time. So we stand adjourned until tomorrow at 2.15 in the afternoon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 18th day of January, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 22 23 24 25
